//: The ZK artefact bundle a REMOTE build downloads, pinned by content.
examples/passport-balancer/contracts-stagenet/managed/*/{keys,zkir} is
~97 MB of prover keys and ZKIR that is deliberately not in git. It is
downloaded because the machines that need it do not have a compiler — not
because it cannot be rebuilt. Until 2026/09/10 this note said the opposite:
the manifests named compactc 0.33.0-rc.2, that release does not exist in
midnightntwrk/compact (the published set goes 0.31.1 then 0.34.0), and a
different compiler was taken to mean different verifier keys.
Measured on 2026/09/10, it does not: compactc 0.34.0 reproduces every one
of these verifier keys BIT-IDENTICALLY to the 0.33.0-rc.2 keys the stagenet
contracts were deployed with — `cmp` clean on all 23 of them, across the
language bump to 0.26 that 0.34.0 requires and the runtime bump to 0.19.0.
Neither the Vercel builder nor verify-demo.yml installs `compact`, so the
bundle still travels as a release asset; a developer who has the toolchain
rebuilds instead and fetch-zk-artefacts.mjs downloads nothing.
This file pins WHICH bytes.
scripts/fetch-zk-artefacts.mjs refuses anything whose sha256 or length
does not match, and then hands the extracted tree to the workflow's
verify-zk-artefacts.mjs, which checks every file against the tracked
compiler/contract-manifest.json. The pin is the supply chain; the
manifests are the correctness.
WHEN THE CONTRACTS ARE REBUILT: cut the release with the new bundle, then
replace `tag`, `sha256`, and `bytes` here in the same commit that lands the
new manifests. A stale pin fails at the manifest check, loudly, before
anything is built.
THE PIN NAMES THIS REPOSITORY NOW (2026/09/15). It named
midnightntwrk/passport v11 until today, and that release no longer exists
— `gh release view v11 --repo midnightntwrk/passport` answers `release not
found`, so every remote build and every workflow that fell back to the pin
was fetching a 404. Releases are cut here, on midnightntwrk/passport-demo,
which is also the repository the Foundation watches, so the pin follows
them. Pinned to v16 (2026/09/15), verified against the published asset:

Releases are named v<major>.<minor> from 2026/09/15; v16 is the last of the legacy undotted ones, and the pin stays on it because it exists and carries the bundle. It moves to v1.0 once that release exists.
THE BUNDLE CARRIES account AND midnames, AND NOT account-k1 (2026/09/16).
The k1-arm build landed with its contract/ and compiler/ halves tracked
like every other build's and its artefacts in no release. That is a gap
rather than a break: verify-zk-artefacts.mjs skips a contract that shipped
neither keys/ nor zkir/, prepare-zk-assets.mjs stages its module and says
the artefacts are absent, and nothing in the app asks for the module. When
something does, the next release's bundle must carry
managed/account-k1/{keys,zkir} and this pin must move to it. Measure first:
that keys/ directory is 3.2 GB against the 110 MB the whole bundle is now.
Overridable for a one-off with PASSPORT_ZK_BUNDLE_TAG,
PASSPORT_ZK_BUNDLE_SHA256, and PASSPORT_ZK_BUNDLE_REPO.
